reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
It's the third week of August. The summer is starting to lean toward its end, and there's a specific kind of Tuesday that shows up this time of year — nothing dramatic, nothing to post about, just a regular workday with regular light. When I was drinking, I couldn't stand these days. They felt like filler. Something to endure until the weekend gave me permission to feel alive again.

What sobriety actually gave me — and this took years to understand — wasn't more big days. It was the ability to be inside the small ones. To notice that the coffee is good. That my body isn't hurting. That I answered a text I would have avoided for a week. That I'm the kind of person now who does the dishes before bed because I know I'll want a clean sink in the morning. None of that fits on a chip, but all of it is the actual life.

Durant's line, riffing on Aristotle, gets it right. The person I've become wasn't built on the mountaintop days — the ski trips, the trips abroad, the big anniversaries. Those were the reward. The person was built on the Tuesdays. On showing up sober for the ordinary hour in front of me, over and over, until ordinary stopped feeling like a punishment and started feeling like home.
reflection.meditation: Today, let the ordinary be enough. Notice one small thing you would have missed drunk.

affirmations: I am building a life on ordinary days, not just on the good ones.
Today I get to be present for whatever this Tuesday actually is.
I am becoming someone I can live with, one honest hour at a time.

gratitude.prayer: I'm grateful for a quiet morning and a clear head to meet it with. I'm grateful for the version of me who kept going through the years when nothing about this felt like a gift yet — because he's the reason I get today. And I'm grateful for the small stuff: coffee that tastes like coffee, a body that works, a phone I'm not afraid to check.
gratitude.closing: One more ordinary day. That's the whole thing.
